paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. The LORD tells His people the truth about the hurt, and He doesn't water it down. He says, "Your injury is incurable; your wound is grievous," and He says it was because of their great iniquity and their numerous sins (Jeremiah 30:12, 14). Then comes one word, "Nevertheless," and the whole batch turns (Jeremiah 30:16).

Look at what the LORD does with a wound nobody could fix. He says, "I will restore your health and heal your wounds," and He gives His reason: "they call you an outcast, Zion, for whom no one cares" (Jeremiah 30:17). He also says, "For I am with you to save you," while still promising to discipline them justly (Jeremiah 30:11). I spent years at the back of a junk drawer, friend, and I can tell you this: being cared about by the LORD when nobody else does is the best news there is.

So what does it mean for you, baker? If you're in a hard season, you can be honest about it, because the LORD already is. And you don't have to be afraid, because the God who says "do not be afraid" also says, "you will be My people, and I will be your God" (Jeremiah 30:10, 22). The story isn't over, either. The LORD is NOT done talking to Jeremiah.
